diagnosis-of-exclusion.short: A diagnosis reached by ruling out every other likely cause, because no single test can confirm it.

prolonged-maladaptation.short: The body's control systems (hormones, nerves, mood) stay out of balance for a long time instead of adapting to the training.

under-recovery.short: Too little recovery for the stress you carry, from training or from outside it, so tiredness builds up faster than it clears.

cytokine.short: A small signalling protein from immune and other cells. Some (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) raise inflammation and tell the brain the body is under strain.

hpa-axis.short: The brain's stress chain: the hypothalamus signals the pituitary gland, which sends ACTH to the adrenal glands, which release cortisol.

acth.short: Adrenocorticotropic hormone: made by the pituitary gland, it tells the adrenal glands to release cortisol.

prolactin.short: A hormone from the pituitary gland. Its blood level rises with hard exercise and stress, so it is used as a marker of the stress chain.

biomarker.short: A measurable sign, such as a blood or saliva level or a test result, that stands for a body state or a condition.

two-bout-test.short: Two maximal exercise tests a few hours apart (4 h in the studies here). How performance and hormones change from test 1 to test 2 is read for signs of overreaching.

poms.short: Profile of Mood States: a 65-item questionnaire on tension, depression, anger, vigor, fatigue and confusion, added up to a global mood score.

restq.short: Recovery-Stress Questionnaire for Athletes: 77 items on how stressed you feel and how well you are recovering.

heart-rate-recovery.short: How far heart rate falls in the first minutes after exercise stops. A bigger fall usually means more vagal (parasympathetic) activity.

progressive-overload.short: Raising training load in steps, so each step sits a little above what the body handles now and it can adapt before the next one.

training-monotony.short: How little the daily load varies in a week: the daily mean divided by the standard deviation of the daily loads. High means every day looks alike.

training-strain.short: Weekly training load multiplied by training monotony. It is high when a big week is also a monotonous one.
